definition.def: If you remove something from a place, you take it away. [written]
examples: As soon as the cake is done, remove it from the oven. [VERB noun + from]
At least three bullets were removed from his wounds. [VERB noun from noun]
Often, the simplest answer is just to remove yourself from the situation. [VERB noun from noun]
He went to the refrigerator and removed a bottle of milk. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you remove clothing, you take it off. [written]
If you remove a stain from something, you make the stain disappear by treating it with a chemical or by washing it.
examples: This treatment removes the most stubborn stains. [VERB noun]
Try using lemon juice to remove tobacco stains from your fingers. [VERB noun from noun]

definition.def: If people remove someone from power or from something such as a committee, they stop them being in power or being a member of the committee.
examples: The student senate voted to remove Fuller from office. [VERB noun + from]
The president could only be removed from power once free elections were organised. [VERB noun from noun]
All senior officers involved in the coup will have to be removed. [be VERB-ed]

definition.def: If you remove an obstacle, a restriction, or a problem, you get rid of it.
examples: The agreement removes the last serious obstacle to the signing of the arms treaty. [VERB noun]
Most of her fears had been removed. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you do or experience something at one remove, you do not do it or experience it yourself, but someone else does it or experiences it instead of you. [mainly British]
examples: She enjoyed his company and the excitement of feeling herself linked at one remove to London society.
She can know the world only at several removes.
